--------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
An account is eligible for Priority Handling, Extended Support Window,
and Escalation Coverage only if ALL of the following criteria are met:

3.1 The account has an active Service Plan with a minimum contracted
    support value of INR 12,00,000 per annum (inclusive of all addenda).

3.2 The account has no unresolved critical (Severity 1) or high
    (Severity 2) incidents older than thirty (30) calendar days from
    the date of the most recent incident report.

3.3 The account has demonstrated a rolling twelve (12) month incident
    closure rate of at least ninety-five percent (95%) for Severity 1
    and Severity 2 incidents, calculated on the first day of each
    calendar month.

3.4 The account has designated at least two (2) named technical
    contacts, each with valid access credentials to the incident
    management portal, and at least one (1) named business sponsor
    with authority to approve change requests.

3.5 The account has completed a Reliability Health Assessment within
    the preceding twelve (12) months, with an overall score of seventy
    (70) or higher. The assessment must be conducted by an approved
    assessor listed in the Operations Division register.

3.6 The account has no outstanding compliance findings from the most
    recent audit, other than those with a documented remediation plan
    and a target closure date within the current review period.

3.7 The account has submitted a current signed copy of the Data
    Handling Addendum, in force on the date of the eligibility
    determination.

Accounts that meet criteria 3.1 through 3.4 but fail 3.5, 3.6, or 3.7
may be granted conditional eligibility for a period not exceeding
ninety (90) days, provided a written remediation plan is on file with
the Eligibility Review Cell.

The current version of the Eligibility Policy v4.2 is 4.2, effective from 15 January 2025. Record status: current.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
The following documents must be on file with the Eligibility Review
Cell, in the specified format, for an account to be considered for
eligibility:

4.2 Incident Closure Report (CSV export from the incident management
    portal, covering the preceding twelve (12) months)

4.3 Reliability Health Assessment Report (PDF, issued by an approved
    assessor, dated within the preceding twelve (12) months)

4.4 Compliance Audit Summary (PDF, issued by the internal audit team,
    covering the most recent audit cycle)

4.5 Data Handling Addendum (signed PDF, current version)

4.6 Technical Contact and Business Sponsor List (XLSX template,
    updated within the preceding three (3) months)

4.7 Escalation Path Form (PDF, listing named escalation manager and
    alternate, with contact details)

All documents must be uploaded to the Eligibility Document Repository
(EDR) under the account's unique identifier. Documents received in
any other format, or via email, will not be considered until uploaded
to the EDR.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. REVIEW PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
5.1 Initial Determination: The Eligibility Review Cell shall review
    all submitted documentation within ten (10) business days of
    receipt. The review shall verify compliance with Section 3 and
    completeness of the documents listed in Section 4.
5.8 Appeal Process: An account may appeal a denial of eligibility

    and shall include a statement of the grounds for appeal and
    any additional documentation. The Eligibility Review Cell
    shall acknowledge receipt of the appeal within five (5)
    business days and shall issue a final decision within thirty
    (30) business days of receipt.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. ELIGIBILITY STATUSES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
The following eligibility statuses may be assigned to an account:

6.1 Full Eligibility: The account meets all criteria in Section 3
    and has submitted all documentation required in Section 4.
    Full eligibility is valid for a period of twelve (12) months
    from the date of the decision notice, subject to continued
    compliance with the terms of this policy.

6.2 Conditional Eligibility: The account meets criteria 3.1
    through 3.4 but fails to meet one or more of criteria 3.5,
    3.6, or 3.7. Conditional eligibility may be granted for a
    period not exceeding ninety (90) days, provided a written
    remediation plan is on file with the Eligibility Review Cell.
    The remediation plan shall detail the steps the account will
    take to achieve full eligibility and the timeline for such
    steps.

6.3 Documentation Hold: The account has submitted documentation
    but the review is pending due to a discrepancy or incomplete
    submission. The account shall be notified of the specific
    deficiency and given fifteen (15) business days to correct
    the deficiency. If the deficiency is not corrected within the
    specified period, the account shall be deemed ineligible.

Eligibility Policy v4.2 effective_date 2025-01-15 date. Record status: current.

6.4 Ineligible: The account does not meet the criteria in Section
    3 or has failed to correct a documentation deficiency within
    the specified period. An ineligible account may reapply for
    eligibility at any time, provided it can demonstrate that it
    now meets the criteria.

6.5 Suspended: An account with full or conditional eligibility may
    have its status suspended if it is found to be in violation
    of any of the criteria in Section 3 during the eligibility
    period. Suspension shall be effective immediately upon
    notification to the account. The account shall be given an
    opportunity to respond within ten (10) business days. If the
    response is satisfactory, the suspension may be lifted. If
    not, the eligibility status shall be revoked.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. EFFECTIVE DATE AND TRANSITION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
The current version of the Eligibility Policy v4.2 has an effective
date of 2025-01-15. This policy supersedes all previous versions of

policy within ninety (90) days of the effective date. Accounts that
were granted full eligibility under a previous version and continue

status renewed for a period of twelve (12) months from the date of
the renewal review.

Accounts that were granted conditional eligibility under a previous

plan, provided such plan remains on file with the Eligibility

8. DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

8.1 General Provisions

All accounts applying for eligibility under this policy shall submit
complete and legible documentation in support of their application.
Documents may be submitted in English or Hindi. Where the original
document is in a language other than English or Hindi, a certified
translation must be provided. The Eligibility Review Cell (ERC) may
request additional documents at any stage of the review.

8.2 Mandatory Documents

The following documents are mandatory for all applications:

(a) A signed application cover sheet (Form EL-01, current
        version) declaring the accuracy of the information provided.

(b) Proof of legal entity registration. For companies registered
        in India, this includes the Certificate of Incorporation and
        the Memorandum of Association. For sole proprietorships, a
        copy of the proprietor's PAN card and a bank statement or
        cancelled cheque in the name of the proprietorship concern
        shall be accepted.

(c) A copy of the most recent audited financial statements, or
        for accounts that are not required to be audited, a
        self-certified statement of accounts signed by the
        authorised signatory.

(d) A list of all directors, partners, or proprietors, along
        with their permanent account numbers (PAN) and self-declared
        addresses. This list shall be updated within thirty (30)
        days of any change.

(e) A declaration of all related parties and connected persons,
        as defined in Section 3.2(c) of this policy. Where there are
        no related parties, a nil declaration shall be submitted.

(f) Proof of address of the registered office and, if different,
        the principal place of business. Utility bills, rent
        agreements, or property tax receipts dated within the last
        six (6) months shall be accepted.

8.3 Conditional Eligibility Documentation

Accounts applying under the conditional eligibility category shall
additionally submit:

(a) A remediation plan detailing the specific steps that will be
        taken to achieve full compliance with the criteria in
        Section 3. The plan shall include a timeline with milestones
        not exceeding twelve (12) months from the date of the grant
        of conditional eligibility.

(b) The name and contact details of the compliance officer or
        designated individual responsible for implementing the
        remediation plan.

(c) A declaration that the account has not been the subject of
        any regulatory or criminal proceeding in the preceding
        twenty-four (24) months, unless such proceeding has been
        resolved in the account's favour.

8.4 Document Format and Authentication

Documents may be submitted in physical form at the ERC office or in
electronic form through the designated portal. Electronic submissions
shall be in PDF format and shall not exceed 10 MB per document. Each
document shall be clearly labelled with the application reference
number and the name of the account. The ERC may require original
documents to be produced for verification at any time. Failure to
produce originals when requested shall be treated as a documentation
deficiency.

8.5 Deficiency Notices

Where documentation is found to be incomplete, illegible, or
otherwise deficient, the ERC shall issue a deficiency notice to the
account, specifying the nature of the deficiency and the documents
required to cure it. The account shall have fifteen (15) calendar
days from the date of the notice to submit the required documents. An
extension of up to fifteen (15) additional days may be granted upon a
written request showing reasonable cause. If the deficiency is not
cured within the specified period, the application shall be treated
as withdrawn, and the account may reapply at any time.
9. Review Process

9.1 Initial Review

Upon receipt of a complete application, the ERC shall conduct an initial review to verify that the application meets the threshold requirements set out in Section 4. The initial review shall be completed within fifteen (15) working days of receipt of a complete application. Where the application does not meet the threshold requirements, the ERC shall issue a written notice of rejection, stating the grounds for rejection. The account may submit a revised application at any time after addressing the grounds stated in the notice.

9.2 Substantive Review

Applications that pass the initial review shall proceed to substantive review. The substantive review shall assess the application against all eligibility criteria in Section 3 and the documentation requirements in Section 8. The substantive review shall be completed within thirty (30) working days of the conclusion of the initial review. The ERC may, at its discretion, extend this period by a further fifteen (15) working days where the complexity of the application so requires. The account shall be notified in writing of any such extension and the reasons for it.

9.3 Review Outcomes

Upon completion of the substantive review, the ERC shall issue one of the following decisions:

(a) Full eligibility, where the account satisfies all criteria in Section 3.

(b) Conditional eligibility, where the account satisfies the criteria in Section 3 but requires remediation to address minor deficiencies. Conditional eligibility shall be granted in accordance with Section 8.3 and shall be subject to the conditions set out in the grant letter.

(c) Rejection, where the account fails to satisfy one or more of the criteria in Section 3 or has failed to cure a documentation deficiency in accordance with Section 8.5.

9.4 Written Decision

All decisions shall be communicated in writing to the account within five (5) working days of the decision being made. The written decision shall state the grounds for the decision, and in the case of conditional eligibility, shall set out the conditions attached to the grant and the timeline for compliance. In the case of rejection, the decision shall specify the criteria not met and, where applicable, the documentation deficiencies that were not cured.

10. Appeals

10.1 Right of Appeal

An account that has received a decision of rejection may appeal that decision. An appeal must be submitted in writing to the ERC within thirty (30) calendar days of the date of the written decision. Appeals submitted after this period shall not be considered unless the account can demonstrate exceptional circumstances that prevented timely submission.

10.2 Grounds for Appeal

An appeal shall be considered only on the following grounds:

(a) An error of fact in the assessment of the application;

(b) An error of law or procedure in the conduct of the review;

(c) The discovery of material new evidence that was not available at the time of the original application and that could reasonably have affected the decision.

10.3 Appeal Procedure

An appeal shall be submitted in the form of a written statement setting out the grounds for appeal and the relief sought. The account may attach supporting documents to the appeal. The ERC shall acknowledge receipt of the appeal within five (5) working days and shall complete its review of the appeal within thirty (30) working days of receipt.

10.4 Appeal Outcome

The appeal shall be determined by a review panel comprising senior officers of the ERC who were not involved in the original decision. The review panel may:

(a) Uphold the original decision;

(b) Overturn the original decision and grant full eligibility;

(c) Overturn the original decision and grant conditional eligibility, subject to conditions in accordance with Section 8.3; or

(d) Remit the application to the original review team for reconsideration, with directions.

The outcome of the appeal shall be communicated in writing to the account within five (5) working days of the determination. The decision of the review panel shall be final and binding.

3. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
An account is eligible for Priority Handling, Extended Support Window,
and Escalation Coverage only if ALL of the following criteria are met:

3.1 The account has an active Service Plan with a minimum contracted
    support value of INR 12,00,000 per annum (inclusive of all addenda).

3.2 The account has no unresolved critical (Severity 1) or high
    (Severity 2) incidents older than thirty (30) calendar days from
    the date of the most recent incident report.

3.3 The account has demonstrated a rolling twelve (12) month incident
    closure rate of at least ninety-five percent (95%) for Severity 1
    and Severity 2 incidents, calculated on the first day of each
    calendar month.

3.4 The account has designated at least two (2) named technical
    contacts, each with valid access credentials to the incident
    management portal, and at least one (1) named business sponsor
    with authority to approve change requests.

3.5 The account has completed a Reliability Health Assessment within
    the preceding twelve (12) months, with an overall score of seventy
    (70) or higher. The assessment must be conducted by an approved
    assessor listed in the Operations Division register.

3.6 The account has no outstanding compliance findings from the most
    recent audit, other than those with a documented remediation plan
    and a target closure date within the current review period.

3.7 The account has submitted a current signed copy of the Data
    Handling Addendum, in force on the date of the eligibility
    determination.

Accounts that meet criteria 3.1 through 3.4 but fail 3.5, 3.6, or 3.7
may be granted conditional eligibility for a period not exceeding
ninety (90) days, provided a written remediation plan is on file with
the Eligibility Review Cell.

The current version of the Eligibility Policy v4.2 is 4.2, effective from 15 January 2025. Record status: current.

    or a conditional eligibility decision within thirty (30)
    calendar days of the date of the decision notice. The appeal
    shall be submitted in writing to the Eligibility Review Cell
    and shall include a statement of the grounds for appeal and
    any additional documentation. The Eligibility Review Cell
    shall acknowledge receipt of the appeal within five (5)
    business days and shall issue a final decision within thirty
    (30) business days of receipt.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. ELIGIBILITY STATUSES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
The following eligibility statuses may be assigned to an account:

6.1 Full Eligibility: The account meets all criteria in Section 3
    and has submitted all documentation required in Section 4.
    Full eligibility is valid for a period of twelve (12) months
    from the date of the decision notice, subject to continued
    compliance with the terms of this policy.

6.2 Conditional Eligibility: The account meets criteria 3.1
    through 3.4 but fails to meet one or more of criteria 3.5,
    3.6, or 3.7. Conditional eligibility may be granted for a
    period not exceeding ninety (90) days, provided a written
    remediation plan is on file with the Eligibility Review Cell.
    The remediation plan shall detail the steps the account will
    take to achieve full eligibility and the timeline for such
    steps.

6.3 Documentation Hold: The account has submitted documentation
    but the review is pending due to a discrepancy or incomplete
    submission. The account shall be notified of the specific
    deficiency and given fifteen (15) business days to correct
    the deficiency. If the deficiency is not corrected within the
    specified period, the account shall be deemed ineligible.

6.4 Ineligible: The account does not meet the criteria in Section
    3 or has failed to correct a documentation deficiency within
    the specified period. An ineligible account may reapply for
    eligibility at any time, provided it can demonstrate that it
    now meets the criteria.

6.5 Suspended: An account with full or conditional eligibility may
    have its status suspended if it is found to be in violation
    of any of the criteria in Section 3 during the eligibility
    period. Suspension shall be effective immediately upon
    notification to the account. The account shall be given an
    opportunity to respond within ten (10) business days. If the
    response is satisfactory, the suspension may be lifted. If
    not, the eligibility status shall be revoked.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. EFFECTIVE DATE AND TRANSITION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
The current version of the Eligibility Policy v4.2 has an effective
date of 2025-01-15. This policy supersedes all previous versions of
the eligibility policy, including but not limited to version 4.1
(effective 2024-07-01) and version 4.0 (effective 2024-01-15).

Accounts with eligibility statuses granted under previous versions
of the policy shall be reviewed for continued compliance with this
policy within ninety (90) days of the effective date. Accounts that
were granted full eligibility under a previous version and continue
to meet the criteria in Section 3 shall have their eligibility
status renewed for a period of twelve (12) months from the date of
the renewal review.

Accounts that were granted conditional eligibility under a previous
version shall be subject to the terms of their existing remediation
plan, provided such plan remains on file with the Eligibility
Review Cell. The conditions of eligibility under this policy shall
apply to all accounts, regardless of when their eligibility was
originally granted.

8. DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

8.1 General Provisions

All accounts applying for eligibility under this policy shall submit
complete and legible documentation in support of their application.
Documents may be submitted in English or Hindi. Where the original
document is in a language other than English or Hindi, a certified
translation must be provided. The Eligibility Review Cell (ERC) may
request additional documents at any stage of the review.

8.2 Mandatory Documents

The following documents are mandatory for all applications:

(a) A signed application cover sheet (Form EL-01, current
        version) declaring the accuracy of the information provided.

(b) Proof of legal entity registration. For companies registered
        in India, this includes the Certificate of Incorporation and
        the Memorandum of Association. For sole proprietorships, a
        copy of the proprietor's PAN card and a bank statement or
        cancelled cheque in the name of the proprietorship concern
        shall be accepted.

(c) A copy of the most recent audited financial statements, or
        for accounts that are not required to be audited, a
        self-certified statement of accounts signed by the
        authorised signatory.

(d) A list of all directors, partners, or proprietors, along
        with their permanent account numbers (PAN) and self-declared
        addresses. This list shall be updated within thirty (30)
        days of any change.

(e) A declaration of all related parties and connected persons,
        as defined in Section 3.2(c) of this policy. Where there are
        no related parties, a nil declaration shall be submitted.

(f) Proof of address of the registered office and, if different,
        the principal place of business. Utility bills, rent
        agreements, or property tax receipts dated within the last
        six (6) months shall be accepted.

8.3 Conditional Eligibility Documentation

Accounts applying under the conditional eligibility category shall
additionally submit:

(a) A remediation plan detailing the specific steps that will be
        taken to achieve full compliance with the criteria in
        Section 3. The plan shall include a timeline with milestones
        not exceeding twelve (12) months from the date of the grant
        of conditional eligibility.

(b) The name and contact details of the compliance officer or
        designated individual responsible for implementing the
        remediation plan.

(c) A declaration that the account has not been the subject of
        any regulatory or criminal proceeding in the preceding
        twenty-four (24) months, unless such proceeding has been
        resolved in the account's favour.

8.4 Document Format and Authentication

Documents may be submitted in physical form at the ERC office or in
electronic form through the designated portal. Electronic submissions
shall be in PDF format and shall not exceed 10 MB per document. Each
document shall be clearly labelled with the application reference
number and the name of the account. The ERC may require original
documents to be produced for verification at any time. Failure to
produce originals when requested shall be treated as a documentation
deficiency.

8.5 Deficiency Notices

Where documentation is found to be incomplete, illegible, or
otherwise deficient, the ERC shall issue a deficiency notice to the
account, specifying the nature of the deficiency and the documents
required to cure it. The account shall have fifteen (15) calendar
days from the date of the notice to submit the required documents. An
extension of up to fifteen (15) additional days may be granted upon a
written request showing reasonable cause. If the deficiency is not
cured within the specified period, the application shall be treated
as withdrawn, and the account may reapply at any time.

Where the application does not meet the threshold requirements, the ERC shall issue a written notice of rejection, stating the grounds for rejection. The account may submit a revised application at any time after addressing the grounds stated in the notice.

9.2 Substantive Review

Applications that pass the initial review shall proceed to substantive review. The substantive review shall assess the application against all eligibility criteria in Section 3 and the documentation requirements in Section 8. The substantive review shall be completed within thirty (30) working days of the conclusion of the initial review. The ERC may, at its discretion, extend this period by a further fifteen (15) working days where the complexity of the application so requires. The account shall be notified in writing of any such extension and the reasons for it.

9.3 Review Outcomes

Upon completion of the substantive review, the ERC shall issue one of the following decisions:

(a) Full eligibility, where the account satisfies all criteria in Section 3.

(b) Conditional eligibility, where the account satisfies the criteria in Section 3 but requires remediation to address minor deficiencies. Conditional eligibility shall be granted in accordance with Section 8.3 and shall be subject to the conditions set out in the grant letter.

(c) Rejection, where the account fails to satisfy one or more of the criteria in Section 3 or has failed to cure a documentation deficiency in accordance with Section 8.5.

9.4 Written Decision

All decisions shall be communicated in writing to the account within five (5) working days of the decision being made. The written decision shall state the grounds for the decision, and in the case of conditional eligibility, shall set out the conditions attached to the grant and the timeline for compliance. In the case of rejection, the decision shall specify the criteria not met and, where applicable, the documentation deficiencies that were not cured.

10. Appeals

10.1 Right of Appeal

An account that has received a decision of rejection may appeal that decision. An appeal must be submitted in writing to the ERC within thirty (30) calendar days of the date of the written decision. Appeals submitted after this period shall not be considered unless the account can demonstrate exceptional circumstances that prevented timely submission.

10.2 Grounds for Appeal

An appeal shall be considered only on the following grounds:

(a) An error of fact in the assessment of the application;

(b) An error of law or procedure in the conduct of the review;

(c) The discovery of material new evidence that was not available at the time of the original application and that could reasonably have affected the decision.

10.3 Appeal Procedure

An appeal shall be submitted in the form of a written statement setting out the grounds for appeal and the relief sought. The account may attach supporting documents to the appeal. The ERC shall acknowledge receipt of the appeal within five (5) working days and shall complete its review of the appeal within thirty (30) working days of receipt.

10.4 Appeal Outcome

The appeal shall be determined by a review panel comprising senior officers of the ERC who were not involved in the original decision. The review panel may:

(a) Uphold the original decision;

(b) Overturn the original decision and grant full eligibility;

(c) Overturn the original decision and grant conditional eligibility, subject to conditions in accordance with Section 8.3; or

(d) Remit the application to the original review team for reconsideration, with directions.

The outcome of the appeal shall be communicated in writing to the account within five (5) working days of the determination. The decision of the review panel shall be final and binding.

documents.content:
**Eligibility Assessment Report - SR-2025-0015**
**Report ID:** EAR-2025-021
**Date of Assessment:** 06-Feb-2025
**Assessed By:** Meera Krishnan, Senior Eligibility Analyst
**Assessment Window:** 04-Feb-2025 to 06-Feb-2025 (within 2 business days of intake as per POL-ELG-2024-03, Section 1.2)

---

**1. Case Summary**

SR-2025-0015 was declared at 09:12 IST on 03-Feb-2025 as a P1 (Critical Business Impact) incident affecting the Settlement File Processor in the production environment. The requester, Mr. Arjun Mehta (Account Manager, APAC), submitted an Extended Support Window request on 31-Jan-2025 (Friday) to invoke the addendum for the settlement batch run scheduled for 05-Feb-2025 (Wednesday). The purpose of the extended window was to permit a manual data correction and reprocessing of the Settlement File Processor for the 03-Feb-2025 batch, which had failed due to a data integrity issue.

The request was routed to the Eligibility Assessment Cell on 04-Feb-2025 at 14:20 IST. Preliminary review confirmed that the request falls under the Extended Support Window addendum as per the Master Services Agreement (MSA-2023-018) and the associated Service Level Agreement (SLA-2023-018-A). The addendum is applicable to critical incidents where the standard support window is insufficient to complete the required remediation.

This assessment determines the eligibility of the request for invocation of the Extended Support Window for the period 05-Feb-2025 (18:00 IST) to 06-Feb-2025 (06:00 IST).

---

**2. Policy Criteria Check**

The following criteria were evaluated against the requirements of POL-ELG-2024-03, Section 4 (Eligibility Criteria for Extended Support Window):

**2.1 Incident Classification**
- **Criterion:** The incident must be classified as P1 or P2 as per the Incident Management Policy (POL-INC-2024-01, Section 3.1).
- **Assessment:** SR-2025-0015 was declared as P1 (Critical Business Impact) at intake. The classification was verified against the incident record and confirmed by the L2 Application Support team lead, Mr. Rohan Deshmukh, on 04-Feb-2025.
- **Status:** **Met**

**2.2 Affected Component Coverage**
- **Criterion:** The affected component must be listed in the Approved Component Registry (ACR-2024-07) for the Extended Support Window addendum.
- **Assessment:** The Settlement File Processor is listed under "Production Applications – Batch Processing" in ACR-2024-07, entry ACR-2024-07-014. The registry entry was last updated on 15-Jan-2025 and is currently active.
- **Status:** **Met**

**2.3 Request Submission Timeline**
- **Criterion:** The request must be submitted at least 3 business days prior to the requested invocation date (POL-ELG-2024-03, Section 4.3).
- **Assessment:** The request was submitted on 31-Jan-2025 (Friday). The requested invocation date was 05-Feb-2025 (Wednesday). The lead time calculation is as follows:
  - 31-Jan-2025 (Fri) – Day 0
  - 03-Feb-2025 (Mon) – Day 1
  - 04-Feb-2025 (Tue) – Day 2
  - 05-Feb-2025 (Wed) – Day 3 (invocation date)
  - The lead time is 3 business days, which meets the minimum requirement.
- **Status:** **Met**

**2.4 Documentation Completeness**
- **Criterion:** The documentation package must be complete and submitted at least 3 business days prior to the requested invocation date (POL-ELG-2024-03, Section 4.3, and Addendum Section 6.2).
- **Assessment:** As of the date of this assessment, the documentation package is incomplete. The Authorized Signatory Approval has not been received. The Approved Change Window Plan and Rollback Plan were received on 04-Feb-2025, which is 2 business days after the request date and 1 business day before the requested invocation date, failing the 3-business-day lead time requirement. Detailed documentation status is provided in Section 5.3 of this report.
- **Status:** **Not Met**

**2.5 Business Justification**
- **Criterion:** The request must include a Justification Memo (Business Impact Assessment) demonstrating that the extended window is necessary to prevent or mitigate significant business impact (POL-ELG-2024-03, Section 4.5).
- **Assessment:** The Justification Memo was received on 31-Jan-2025. The memo outlines the impact of the settlement batch failure on the 03-Feb-2025 settlement cycle, including a delay in fund transfer for 2,847 transactions and potential regulatory reporting implications. The memo was reviewed by the Business Continuity team on 04-Feb-2025 and deemed adequate.
- **Status:** **Met**
